subject: Isolated lanes, sizing & SLA proposal — follow-up from Wednesday call
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@dragonfly.health>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@dragonfly.health>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 06 Jun 2026 15:01:00 -0700
Subject: Isolated lanes, sizing & SLA proposal — follow-up from Wednesday call

Thanks again for a productive call earlier this week — wanted to capture the key points, open questions, and our proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth. High level summary first:

- Pain & goals you shared:
  - Live inference for clinical triage workloads (100–300 qps sustained spike patterns; heavy tail on peak days)
  - Data isolation is required for PHI — you prefer a dedicated pool per environment (prod/stage) with tenant-level network isolation
  - Low tail latency requirement for interactive clinician workflows (p99 token latency target <= 220ms)
  - Cost sensitivity for 24/7 baseline vs. burst capacity for peak hours

- Technical constraints you emphasized:
  - Models: 30B encoder-decoder variant (fine-tuned) with 1.2k seq typical, occasional 4k tokens
  - KV cache hot prefix reuse across sessions (we should preserve to hit latency SLOs)
  - Regulatory: SOC2 evidence + customer-managed KMS for key material

- Our proposed Dedicated approach (short):
  - Two isolated "lanes" (prod + stage) backed by reserved H100 instances with operator-managed VPC peering.
  - Baseline reserve sized for 120 qps sustained (A100-equivalent throughput) with burst pool to shared fleet for short peaks up to 320 qps.
  - Autoscaling policy: margin-based autoscale + burst-to-shared fallback; can cap burst to prevent noisy neighbor impact.
  - SLA target: 99.95% availability with p99 token latency guardrails; escalation path and cross-region fallback if a region is degraded.

Open questions / clarifications we need from Dragonfly (please confirm):
1) Exact production qps baseline you'd commit to for procurement (we used 120 qps in the estimate attached).
2) Max tolerable failover window for regional fallback (we suggested 5 mins for cold start of fallback model pools).
3) Is cross-region replication of KV cache acceptable (adds replication cost) or prefer cold-warm startup?

Attachments: attached a sizing workbook (dragonfly_isolation_sizing_v1.xlsx) with baseline/burst cost sims and a short ops playbook.

Next steps (proposed):
- You: confirm baseline qps and fallback tolerance by Tue 9 Jun
- Us: update sizing + draft committed capacity term sheet (with SLOs & failover) by Thu 11 Jun
- Joint: 30-min ops walk (deep dive into KV cache warmup and container cold-start mitigation) — propose Wed 17 Jun 10am PT

If anything above is off, flag it and we’ll fix. Thanks — Mina

--
Mina Haddad
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0187

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@dragonfly.health>

Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@dragonfly.health>, Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@dragonfly.health>
Date: Mon, 08 Jun 2026 09:07:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Isolated lanes, sizing & SLA proposal — follow-up from Wednesday call

Mina — thanks for the clear write-up. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Baseline: we think 100 qps is a safe committed baseline for procurement right now (we can bump to 140 after Q4 if usage growth matches).
- Failover: 5 minutes is OK for cold-warm startup; for mission-critical clinician flows we need an interim degraded mode that returns a short note (60–80 tokens) rather than failing hard.
- KV replication: cross-region replication is something we want to avoid for now due to PHI concerns; prefer cold-warm with a warming policy (keep top 5k prefixes cached in warm pool).

Also want to confirm GPU type — H100 is fine but if A100 L4 (or similar) reduces cost with acceptable latency we’re open to hybrid configs.

We reviewed the sizing sheet quickly — Priya will drop a procurement timeline by EOD tomorrow (Tue). Can you include a rough draft of the committed monthly spend in the term sheet? We need it for our internal finance review.

Thanks,
Liam

Subject: Re: Isolated lanes, sizing & SLA proposal — follow-up from Wednesday call

Adding a couple of operational notes from the runbook side: 

- Warm pool strategy: we recommend maintaining a small warm fleet (20% of baseline capacity in hot instances) to keep KV cache primed for top prefixes; that should materially reduce p99 latency on bursts.
- Quantization: we can provide a mixed-precision path (int8 quant for non-critical tokens) that typically reduces memory pressure by ~30% — useful if you hit instance memory limits on 4k sequences.
- Observability: per-route token-level tracing and synthetic prompt set monitors (we'll surface regressions to an SLA-linked alert).

I’ll add these into the ops playbook and annotate the workbook with expected latency delta for each mitigation.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
